I'm a physician. While I haven't made any screw ups, I'm human and it's almost inevitable. No one wants to cover up/look past misconduct but sometimes it is truly in everyone's best interest to just move on. One example is radiologist's reports. Radiologists misread scans all the time, some much more than others. One time they missed a 5 inch tumor on my patient. Do they miss every time? No. Yeah there are a few bad apples that don't give their best every time, but the vast majority do and unfortunately are stuck covering for the bad apples in order to serve a greater good of respect for the profession and subsequent patient trust.

There are a few differences for physicians: 1) We're obligated to tell the patient about the mistakes if it has any effect on their care. 2) Physicians hold liability insurance which they will lose if they have a pattern of malpractice.

It's not really about making mistakes, because every human does that, its about how you respond to them.
